phase: Bounded native M1/M2/M4 acceptance through S1-S5
working_tree: Native implementation and documentation remain uncommitted alongside preserved prior M3/M5 and M6 packets.
path_base: Relative paths resolve from rebase-next; target artifacts are retained local observations, regenerable from the fingerprinted sources.
authorization: User requested autonomous completion and explicitly authorized a goal; S1-S5 are one bounded goal. No production/API/distributed expansion.

S1.scope: Independent exact command/source oracle and native-format valid/corrupt/incomplete controls before writer implementation.

S2.scope: Exact values, prepared dependency order, strict commands/codec and typed point workspace; two focused Rust tests plus native fixture binding/version/lifecycle cases.

S3.scope: Financial/quote intrusive AVL operations; all rotation directions, leaf/one-child/two-child/root/last deletion, equal-time grouping and i64 extrema against source scans.

S4.scope: Fixed source/routes/quotes/postings settlement via the same native entrypoint in every observed operation; no whole-store mutation scan or tree rebuild.

S5.scope: Real redb write transactions, complete raw-table observations, old/new snapshots, abort after partial/full actual batch, unchanged rejection maps and same-model reopen.

counter_scope: Fixture operations only, excluding initialization/base installation. Candidates are recorded on entry to evaluation/reconciliation. Encoded bytes exclude keys/deletions/storage internals. Dirty counts on aborted operations describe prepared batches, not committed writes.

static_check_correction.finding: Three collapsible-if warnings in native settlement; fixed without behavioral changes before final acceptance. Final source identity required fresh native observations.

not_claimed: Native M3/M5 prefix/output scheduler or managed-output lifecycle
General model/schema loader or semantic activation protocol
Public RPC, complete developer catalogs, frontend or full accounting port
Principal DAG, real credential verification or general authorization
Minimal interval invalidation or staged range overlay
Receipts, retry/replay, external effects or exactly-once delivery
Distributed guards, concurrency adapter conformance, throughput or capacity
